page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v5 is an enterprise memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources include 16 physical cores across 32 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, supplemented by 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB shared L3 cache. Memory provisioning is substantial at 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The instance does not include local disk storage, requiring network-attached remote disks, and contains zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-to-high-tier performance across memory and CPU-centric workloads. The platform achieved a PassMark memory score of 2,821.07 and Geekbench image processing score of 13,659.0, both placing in the top quartile of tested systems. Memory bandwidth registers 150.25 GB/sec for uncached reads and 67.0 GB/sec for uncached writes, enabling 31.36 million Redis SET operations per second. General computation scores such as PassMark CPU at 36,843.62 and Geekbench multi-core at 14,331.0 fall within the median tier. Large-scale transformer prompt processing for 70B parameter models registers in the bottom quartile at 6.65 tokens per second, reflecting the absence of specialized tensor or GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E32s_v5 presents an advantageous resource balance for applications where memory capacity and high per-thread throughput dictate infrastructure requirements over raw compute or discrete graphics acceleration. Because storage is entirely unbundled, teams avoid paying for unused local NVMe volumes while retaining flexibility to attach appropriate managed disks. The instance is suited for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, large relational databases, enterprise resource planning systems, data processing pipelines, and general memory-heavy production services.
description: Microsoft Azure E32s_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 vCPUs backed by 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz. Equipped with 256 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8 GB per vCPU ratio designed for high memory density. The instance includes no bundled local storage, operating purely with attached remote storage, and features no hardware GPU accelerators. Across benchmarks, the server delivers top-quartile PassMark memory and image processing throughput alongside solid median multi-core computation and 150.25 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. Although CPU-based large language model prompt processing on 70B parameter models remains low, the configuration offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-intensive production workloads without incurring charges for unused local drives. This profile makes the instance well matched for in-memory caches, relational database engines, analytical ETL tasks, and enterprise application tiers.
